refused.forbidden: You may not test the rules of this dataset.
refused.other: The test could not be started. Try again.

test.sampled: Up to {{each}} records of each outcome, ordered by the key.

test.columnsHint: Shown besides the key and the fields the rule reads. A double click moves a column across; Ctrl+click picks several. Applied, the test runs again.
test.groups: Failures by the value's shape (digit = 9, letter = A): {{groups}} shapes, {{shown}} of {{fails}} failures. Choose one to see its records.

editor.otherFile: This draft is another column's: open the file from main to start this one's.
editor.deployed: Deployed to main: the rules are under their field now.
editor.stale: The file changed on main since you opened it: open it again.

file.dataset: The dataset the rules read, as named in its mapping.
file.derived: Fields computed against the cut, never against today.
file.lists: Named lists of values, for domain (in: { list: name }) and in_list(x, 'name').
file.placeholders: Fillers that mean "no value", declared once per type.
file.populations: Named conditions a rule can apply to (population: individuals).
file.references: Other datasets a rule may look up, and which of their cuts.
file.rules: The file's rules, one per item of the list.
file.tables: Tables of allowed or forbidden combinations, for combination.

rule.id: Unique in the dataset (V-PN-01); kept when a rule is imported.
rule.field: The field it checks; a list gives one rule per field.
rule.check: The pattern: what kind of check the rule makes.
rule.severity: How serious a failure is; by default, the pattern's.
rule.cause: Why a record fails: at capture, or in a system that moves the data.
rule.alert: What the person who fixes the record reads.
rule.dimension: Only for expression: the other patterns bring their own.
rule.examples: Records the rule must fail, pass and skip; lint runs them.
rule.fails: In expression: the rule fails where this holds.
rule.if: In implies: when this holds, then must hold.
rule.then: In implies: what must hold when if holds.
rule.both_ways: In implies: then also implies if (an equivalence).
rule.when: The rule applies only where this condition holds.
rule.population: A population declared by the dataset, which the rule applies to.
rule.in: In domain: the allowed values; in length: the allowed lengths.
rule.min: In length and range: the minimum; a number, a date, a field, :cut or an expression.
rule.max: In length and range: the maximum; a number, a date, a field, :cut or an expression.
rule.min_exclusive: In range: the minimum itself is not allowed, only above it.
rule.max_exclusive: In range: the maximum itself is not allowed, only below it.
rule.max_age: In fresh: how old a date may be against the cut (13 months).
rule.pattern: In format: a regular expression, anchored to the whole value.
rule.named: In format: a format maintained by the platform.
rule.values: In placeholder: the fillers to find (default: the dataset's).
rule.parts: In sum: the parts, each with its sign (- Pasivo).
rule.key: In unique: the fields that must not repeat (default: the field).
rule.normalize: In unique and differs: compare normalized values.
rule.ignore: In unique: values that may repeat.
rule.table: In combination: a table declared by the dataset.
rule.case: Texts are compared trimmed and case-insensitive, unless exact.
rule.on_empty: An empty value is skipped by every pattern but required and empty; fail counts it as a failure.
rule.for_each: Repeats the rule for each value: { n: [1, 2] } with TelefonoRef{n}.
rule.origin: Where an imported rule comes from.
rule.note: A note for whoever maintains the rule.

examples.skips: Records the rule must not apply to.

reference.key: The other dataset's field it is looked up by.
reference.where: Only the other dataset's records where this holds (its fields).
reference.as_of: Which cut of the other dataset: by default the same date.

table.when: The field or fields each row starts from.
table.then: The field whose values the rows allow or forbid.
table.rows: The table's rows, one case each.

row.when: One value, several, or * for every other.
row.allowed: The values allowed in that case.
row.forbidden: The values forbidden in that case.

origin.process: The process it was imported from (KNIME).

check.required: Fails if the value is empty or a filler. Completeness.
check.empty: Fails if the value is filled when it must not be. Consistency.
check.placeholder: Fails if the value is a declared filler (ACTUALIZAR, 1900-01-01…). Accuracy.
check.length: Fails if the length is not allowed (in, min, max). Validity.
check.format: Fails if the value does not match pattern (a regular expression) or named. Validity.
check.domain: Fails if the value is not (or is) in a list or a reference: in, not_in. Validity.
check.range: Fails if the value is outside its bounds (min, max). Accuracy.
check.fresh: Fails if a date is older than max_age against the cut. Timeliness.
check.sum: Fails if a total differs from its parts (parts, tolerance). Consistency.
check.unique: Fails if the value repeats across records (key, normalize, ignore). Uniqueness.
check.combination: Fails if a combination of fields is not allowed (table). Consistency.
check.implies: Fails if if holds and then does not. Consistency.
check.differs: Fails if two fields hold the same value (from). Consistency.
check.expression: Fails where a free condition holds (fails). The rule sets its dimension.

severity.blocking: Blocking: the record is unusable until fixed.
severity.minor: Minor: an error of little effect.

cause.capture: It starts where the data is captured.
cause.systemic: It starts in a system that moves or transforms the data.

dimension.consistency: Consistency: the data agrees with other data.
dimension.validity: Validity: the data has an allowed form or value.
dimension.timeliness: Timeliness: the data is up to date.
dimension.uniqueness: Uniqueness: the data does not repeat.

case.insensitive: Ignoring case and surrounding spaces (the default).

on_empty.skip: An empty value is not checked (the default).
on_empty.fail: An empty value counts as a failure.

explorer.filter: Filter by schema, table or column

props.notListed: The last listing does not have this table.

console.more: there are more; narrow the query
console.masked: values masked: you may not see personal data
console.seen: you see the complete values; this read is audited

kind.syntax: The query has a syntax error.
kind.name: A table or column does not exist.
kind.conversion: A value could not be converted to the type asked.
kind.permission: The query tried to read something outside the lake.
kind.engine: The engine could not run the query.

console.formatHint: Lays the statement out: keywords upper case, one clause a line
console.unformattable: It could not be formatted: check its syntax.
console.resize: Resize the rule and the query
console.columnsHint: The result's columns shown, in this order. A double click moves a column across; Ctrl+click picks several. The query is not run again.

delete.title: Delete
delete.dataset: The whole dataset is deleted: its mapping and rules leave main (the catalog's history keeps them), its schedules, cuts and results are deleted, and its lake table with its data. The source's table is not touched and can be mapped again.
delete.table: The lake table is deleted with all its data.

refused.running: {{name}} was not deleted: one of its cuts is being collected or evaluated. Wait for it to end.
refused.in_use: {{name}} was not deleted: a dataset reads it. Delete the dataset.
refused.confirm: Not deleted: the name typed is not {{name}}.
refused.other: {{name}} could not be deleted. Try again.

delete.namespace_one: The lake folder is deleted with its table and all its data.
delete.namespace_other: The lake folder is deleted with its {{count}} tables and all their data.

charts.noCuts: No cut of this dataset has been evaluated yet.
charts.icd_distribution: Distribution of the ICD by entity
charts.pChartNote: Share of records with a serious failure (blocking or major in a critical or high field), by group size. The curves are the control limits.
charts.outliersNote: amounts whose robust z within their group is beyond 3.5, either way
charts.noChange: No change since the previous cut.
charts.stageNote: milliseconds per million record-attributes (records × mapped fields)
charts.stageNoteMs: milliseconds per stage (the cut has no volume to rate them by)
charts.sfcNote: Each row is a cell: a field holding the sfc role, right when filled and no rule that reads it fails. It is 1 when at least 90% of the active records have it right. The band (80–90%) is where the fewest fixes turn a cell from 0 to 1.
charts.queuesNote: Open findings in each group's queue and those past its SLA, counted in days from the cut where each first failed.

slas.title: Remediation SLAs
slas.note: Days each queue has to resolve a finding before it is overdue: a dimension's default, and a group's when set, which wins. A queue with neither has {{days}} days. The queues read them at once: no evaluation is needed.
slas.none: The dataset's mapping has no field with the dimension role: its findings have no queue.
slas.saved: SLAs saved: the queues show them.

refusal.dimension: A dimension is no longer in the dataset's mapping: reload the page.
refusal.days: Days are a whole number from 1 to 365.
refusal.group: A group's value is too long.
refusal.duplicate: A group is set twice in the same dimension.
refusal.too_many: Too many SLAs for one dataset.
refusal.not_found: The dataset has no mapping on main.

reveal.title: Show personal data
reveal.intro: Each showing of values is recorded in the audit with its purpose, its reference, and how many rows and which fields it showed, never a value. The reason is kept in this tab for this scope until you mask again, forget it or sign out.
reveal.referenceHint: A ticket or case number, such as INC-2041: up to 32 characters, letters, digits and - _ / # ., with at least one letter. Never a name or a document number.

invalid.reference: The reference is not a ticket or case number: up to 32 characters, letters, digits and - _ / # ., at least one letter, no spaces.
invalid.required: With Other, write the reference of the ticket or case.

refused.not_found: These values are no longer kept: read them again.
refused.forbidden: You may not see these values whole.
refused.not_done: The values are not ready yet: try again when the read ends.
refused.purpose: That purpose is not accepted: choose another.
refused.reference: The reference was not accepted: check its form (Other requires one).
refused.audit_unavailable: The audit is unavailable, so the values cannot be shown: try again later.
refused.unavailable: The service is unavailable: try again later.
refused.other: The values could not be shown.
